packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-08 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reading)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
the work or author, or any earlier reading. I opened only PROMPT.md and the
image files of this packet. (A directory listing of the packet showed that a
packet.json exists; I did not open it.)

Working notes are appended image by image; the layout survey, selection
statement and limitations are consolidated at the end of this file.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-001.jpg  (reduced overview, face A)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: a very narrow vertical parchment strip (binding waste shape),
photographed upright against black cloth with a cm scale at the foot; the strip
is roughly 0.4-0.6 cm wide and about 16-17 cm tall by the scale. It carries the
middle of c. 30+ horizontal lines of a gothic book hand in brown ink; each line
preserves only about 4-7 letters. The lowest fifth of the strip is blank
(apparently a lower margin), with two small dark marks/holes. A wider blank
band interrupts the text about a fifth of the way down (after the 9th preserved
line). No rubric, running title, initial, underlining or gloss can be seen at
this size; a faint reddish touch appears about three quarters of the way down
(possibly a paragraph mark or red stroke - tentative). No column structure can
be determined from a strip this narrow.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-002.jpg  (native tile, face A, upper part)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Every line is cut at both left and right; readings are letter groups only.
"[" = strip edge on the left, "]" = strip edge on the right.

image-002 l.1   [ ...unli? ]        (top edge, letters cut through the heads; very uncertain)
image-002 l.2   [ alim q? ]         (or "alim q(ue)?")
image-002 l.3   [ ue. ⁊ al? ]       (punctus, then Tironian et)
image-002 l.4   [ ginet? ]          (possibly "(per)tinet?"; first letter has a descender)
image-002 l.5   [ ofuam? ]          (or "o suam?" / "osnam?")
image-002 l.6   [ ag̃s qu ]          (a-g with superscript mark, then "qu"; "(m)ag(i)s qu..."?)
image-002 l.7   [ erne. ]           ("(et)erne."? - punctus after)
image-002 l.8   [ s q(ui)piã? ]     (q with abbreviation stroke, "-piã" with macron; "quippiam?" uncertain)
image-002 l.9   [ aut au ]
                -- blank band, about two line-heights, no ink visible --
image-002 l.10  [ ima Cu? ]         (or "mia Au?"; enlarged/capital letter C or A after a space)
image-002 l.11  [ ꝫ. ſ. ue ]        (letter + punctus, "s." between points = "s(cilicet)"?, then "ue")
image-002 l.12  [ aꝫ ou? ]          (or "uꝫ cu(m)?"; -ꝫ abbreviation)
image-002 l.13  [ lex ã? ]          ("lex" clear; then a letter with macron, "a(n)"/"au"?)
image-002 l.14  [ igꝫ ep? ]         (uncertain; "-igꝫ" then "ep"/"cp")
image-002 l.15  [ o. vetu ]         ("vetu(s)"? - punctus before)
image-002 l.16  [ ue ⁊ le ]         ("...ue et le(x?)")
image-002 l.17  [ ſcimu ]           ("scimu(s)"?)
image-002 l.18  [ c. ⁊ ani? ]       (or "c. Aam?"; punctus, then Tironian et or capital A)
image-002 l.19  [ o. vetu? ]        (or "o. tetu?"; resembles l.15)
image-002 l.20  [ oꝛs bi? ]         (uncertain; "-ors"/"-ois" then "bi")
image-002 l.21  [ lue. q ]          (or "lut. q"; punctus, then q with a stroke)
image-002 l.22  [ omn ]             ("omn(...)")
image-002 l.23  [ ...d? ... ]       (bottom edge of tile, cut)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-003.jpg  (native tile, face A, middle part; overlaps image-002 at its top)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-003 l.1   [ ... ]             (top edge, cut; = image-002 l.18, not new text)
image-003 l.2   [ o. vetu? ]        (= image-002 l.19, overlap; here it looks more like ". tetu"/". vetu")
image-003 l.3   [ ors bi ]          (= image-002 l.20, overlap)
image-003 l.4   [ lue. q ]          (= image-002 l.21, overlap; q with stroke through/after)
image-003 l.5   [ omn? ]            (= image-002 l.22, overlap; "omn"/"omiu")
image-003 l.6   [ ond. Tr? ]        (or "ond. In?"; punctus then a capital, T or I)
image-003 l.7   [ no cele ]         ("...no cele(...)")
image-003 l.8   [ ali. q̃ p ]        ("...ali. q(ui?) p..."; q with superscript mark)
image-003 l.9   [ uiſcꝫ o? ]        (very uncertain; minims + long s? + ꝫ)
image-003 l.10  [ eſtam? ]          (or "ellam"/"ellaui"; "(t)estam(...)"? is a tentative interpretation only)
image-003 l.11  [ ſ. q̃uis? ]        ("s(cilicet?) q(ua)uis?"; uncertain)
image-003 l.12  [ ſtant? ]          (or "ſtare"; small hole at left)
image-003 l.13  [ ſ. eua ]          ("s. eua(n...)"?; possibly capital "Ava")
image-003 l.14  [ lege u? ]         (or "lex ꝑ u"; "leg-" fairly clear)
image-003 l.15  [ nouã ]            ("noua(m)"; macron over a)
image-003 l.16  [ . omnũ? ]         (punctus, then "omn"/"oenu" with macron)
image-003 l.17  [ ũ lꝫ. ? ]         (macron letter, "lꝫ" = "l(icet)"?, punctus; a further letter cut)
image-003 l.18  [ ꝫꝫ. ſig? ]        (uncertain; "...ez. sig(...)")
image-003 l.19  [ lege p̃ ]          (or "ſlex p̃"; p with superscript stroke, "p(re)"/"p(ri)")
image-003 l.20  [ . in u ]
image-003 l.21  [ ic lem? ]         (or "ic ſen"/"ic ſem")
image-003 l.22  [ es. q? ]          (small hole in the middle of the line; punctus, then q or 9-shaped sign)
image-003 l.23  [ ſpondũ? ]         (or "ꝑpo diu"; s/p + "po" + minims with macron)
image-003 l.24  [ niq̃? ]            (minims then "qu"; "(i)niqu(...)"/"inqu(it)?")
image-003 l.25  [ datau? ]          (or "iatau")
image-003 l.26  [ ... ]             (bottom edge, cut through)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-004.jpg  (native tile, face A, lower part; overlaps image-003 at its top)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-004 l.1   [ es. q? ]          (= image-003 l.22, overlap)
image-004 l.2   [ ſpondũ? ]         (= image-003 l.23, overlap)
image-004 l.3   [ niqu? ]           (= image-003 l.24, overlap)
image-004 l.4   [ datau? ]          (= image-003 l.25, overlap)
image-004 l.5   [ [illegible] mo? ] (rubbed; first letter has a descender/flourish)
image-004 l.6   [ ena e? ]          (rubbed; a reddish/pink touch at the right edge - paragraph mark,
                                     red stroke on a capital, or offset; cannot tell)
image-004 l.7   [ uado? ]           (or "icado"; rubbed)
image-004 l.8   [ gem t? ]          (very rubbed; uncertain)
image-004 l.9   [ gat. q ]          (or "ḡat. q"; punctus then q)
image-004 l.10  [ [illegible] ]     (traces only, ink nearly gone)
image-004 l.11  [ nuitau? ]         (minims; last written line, uncertain)
                -- below: blank parchment (lower margin?), three small slits/holes, no ink --

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-005.jpg  (reduced overview, face B)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: a second narrow vertical strip view (same proportions; whether it
is the other face of the strip in image-001 or a different strip cannot be
decided from the images alone - the overall shape, with a blank foot, is
similar). About 40 lines of gothic book hand, 4-7 letters each, ink somewhat
darker and better preserved than face A. About a third of the way down an
enlarged capital "S" sits at the left of a line with a bluish trace beside it
(paragraph mark or pen-flourish residue - tentative). Near the foot, at the left
edge, a small red-and-blue feature (initial or paragraph mark, mostly cut away).
Lowest tenth blank with small holes. No running title or gloss visible.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-006.jpg  (native tile, face B, upper part)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-006 l.1   [ unt? ]            (top edge; or "mir"/"mit")
image-006 l.2   [ ⁊. pe.? ]         (small sign with stroke, punctus, "pe"/"ſe", punctus; uncertain)
image-006 l.3   [ ipſa m? ]         (or "ꝑſa m"; first letters with descender)
image-006 l.4   [ mane ]            (or "inane")
image-006 l.5   [ a ſon? ]          (or "n ſon"/"a ſom")
image-006 l.6   [ actoꝛ ]           ("(f)actor"? - "actor" with round r clear)
image-006 l.7   [ in ing? ]         (or "ini ing"; final letter with descender)
image-006 l.8   [ in ſuu? ]         (or "in ſim")
image-006 l.9   [ in ali ]
image-006 l.10  [ ſebant? ]         (or "ſcbau"/"ſcban"; "-ebant" likely)
image-006 l.11  [ re ſc̃? ]          (or "re ſe"; superscript mark over last letter)
image-006 l.12  [ pⁱma h? ]         (p with superscript i, "ma", then h; "p(ri)ma h..."?)
image-006 l.13  [ ta ſuu? ]         (or "ra ſtu")
image-006 l.14  [ ꝑ. ev? ]          (p with crossed descender, punctus, then "ev"/"en"/"cu")
image-006 l.15  [ ſcd'm u? ]        (or "ſeũ u"; "s(e)c(un)d(u)m u..."? uncertain)
image-006 l.16  [ omnia l? ]        ("om(n)ia" with macron; next letter tall, l/b)
image-006 l.17  [ Scdo ]            (enlarged capital S at left with a blue-green trace beside it;
                                     "S(e)c(un)do"? - a new division opening, tentative)
image-006 l.18  [ re eni? ]         (or "ce cum"/"re cuiu")
image-006 l.19  [ pⁱmaqꝫ? ]         (or "q̃maq"; "p(ri)maq(ue)?" uncertain)
image-006 l.20  [ eſſe m? ]         (or "eſt m"/"ella m")
image-006 l.21  [ q̃ ibu? ]          (q with superscript, then "ibu"/"ibi")
image-006 l.22  [ om̃ del? ]         (or "mi tel"; macron; uncertain)
image-006 l.23  [ ſtimu? ]          (bottom edge, cut)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-007.jpg  (native tile, face B, middle part; overlaps image-006 at its top)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-007 l.1   [ ... ]             (top edge, cut; = image-006 l.19)
image-007 l.2   [ eſſe m? ]         (= image-006 l.20, overlap)
image-007 l.3   [ q̃ ibu? ]          (= image-006 l.21, overlap)
image-007 l.4   [ om̃ del? ]         (= image-006 l.22, overlap; here closer to "ani tel"/"mi del")
image-007 l.5   [ ſtimu? ]          (= image-006 l.23, overlap; minims, "ſlunu"/"ſtimu")
image-007 l.6   [ re ſen? ]         (or "ie ſem")
image-007 l.7   [ muꝰ en? ]         ("-mus" with 9-shaped us-sign; then "en"/"eti")
image-007 l.8   [ uũ in? ]          (minims with macron, then "in"/"m")
image-007 l.9   [ ſlumĩa? ]         (very uncertain; long s/l + minims + macron)
image-007 l.10  [ te qꝛ? ]          ("...te q(uia)?"; q followed by a round-r-like sign; rubbed at right)
image-007 l.11  [ rõne? ]           (or "t nõu"; "r(ati)one"? very uncertain; small hole above)
image-007 l.12  [ alos il? ]        (or "ualoſ il"; small slit in line)
image-007 l.13  [ none ]
image-007 l.14  [ ipꝰ. g? ]         (or "ꝑpꝰ. g"; us-sign, punctus, g)
image-007 l.15  [ ña ver? ]         (or "tia ben"; macron over first letters)
image-007 l.16  [ ginale? ]         (or "ꝑmalo"; "(ori)ginale"? is interpretation only)
image-007 l.17  [ mint? ]           (minims; "uunt"/"mint")
image-007 l.18  [ monte? ]          (or "nonce"/"nontẽ" with a stroke above the end)
image-007 l.19  [ electu? ]         (or "ſc̃ctu"; uncertain)

image-007 l.21  [ nſtitu? ]         (or "inſum"; rubbed)
image-007 l.22  [ . ſp̃e? ]          (punctus, long s, p with mark; "sp(irit)..."/"sp(eci)e"?)
image-007 l.23  [ uanu? ]           (or "liianui"; minims)
image-007 l.24  [ ᵒ. alu? ]         (superscript o + punctus, then "alu"/"ala"; small blue ink trace above
                                     the line at centre-left)
image-007 l.25  [ uunui? ]          (minims only, cut)
image-007 l.26  [ ... ]             (bottom edge, cut)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-008.jpg  (native tile, face B, lower part; overlaps image-007 at its top)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-008 l.1   [ . ſp̃e? ]          (= image-007 l.22, overlap)
image-008 l.2   [ uanu? ]           (= image-007 l.23, overlap)
image-008 l.3   [ ᵒ. alu? ]         (= image-007 l.24, overlap; blue trace above)
image-008 l.4   [ uanus? ]          (= image-007 l.25; or "uirtus"? - minims, uncertain)
image-008 l.5   [ o. vo? ]          (or ". ndi"; rubbed)
image-008 l.6   [ (initial) ſtri? ] (at the left edge the right-hand part of a decorated initial or
                                     paragraph mark, red body with blue pen-work, two lines tall, most of
                                     it cut away; letter not identifiable. Then "ſtri"/"ſci")
image-008 l.7   [ (initial) aſſ? ]  (second line beside the same initial; "aſt"/"aſſ")
image-008 l.8   [ c uit? ]          (or "t tuit"; rubbed)

image-008 l.10  [ is ſui? ]         (or "ls ſtu")

                -- below: blank parchment with a brown vertical stain/fold line and three small slits --

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-009.jpg  (reduced overview, face C)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: a third strip view, same narrow vertical format, but here the TOP
c. 1 cm is blank (upper margin?) and text runs to within c. 1 cm of the foot;
about 45 lines of the same kind of gothic book hand, 5-8 letters per line.
Red features: a red horizontal stroke/paragraph-mark trace at the left edge
about 40% down; a red filled shape (part of an initial or paragraph mark) at the
right edge about 80% down; a red vertical stroke/bracket at the left edge near
the foot beside the last three or four lines. A faint blue trace about 60% down.
Whether this is a different strip from faces A/B or another face of one of them
cannot be decided from the images.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-010.jpg  (native tile, face C, upper part)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Observations
- Four strip views (overviews 001, 005, 009, 013), each with native tiles:
  A = 001 + tiles 002-004; B = 005 + tiles 006-008; C = 009 + tiles 010-012;
  D = 013 + tiles 014-015. Each is a vertical parchment strip c. 0.4-0.6 cm wide
  and c. 16-17 cm tall, cut vertically out of a leaf, so that every line keeps
  only 4-8 letters from somewhere inside the line. Text runs horizontally; the
  strips are upright (script the right way up) in all views.
- Faces A and B have a blank zone only at the foot; faces C and D have blank
  zones at both head and foot. The strip outlines of A and B look alike, and
  those of C and D look broadly alike, so A/B and C/D may be recto/verso pairs of
  two strips - this is a tentative interpretation, not something the images
  state.
- Script: small gothic book hand (textualis, somewhat cursive-leaning in places),
  brown ink, heavily abbreviated (macrons, superscript letters, ꝫ, ꝰ, ꝑ, Tironian
  et, "s." between puncti). About 30 written lines on A, c. 40 on B, c. 45 on C,
  c. 50 on D.
- Decoration/articulation: enlarged capital S with blue trace (006 l.17);
  part of a two-line red initial or paragraph mark with blue pen-work at the left
  edge (008 l.6-7); red horizontal stroke under a line (011 l.6); solid red
  rounded shape at the right edge (012 l.10); red vertical bracket at the left
  edge beside the last two lines (012 l.16-17); red-touched capital S (015 l.21);
  small blue traces (007 l.24, 011 l.20, 015 l.11); a blank band of about two
  lines within face A (after 002 l.9).
- No running titles, no interlinear or marginal glosses, and no clearly
  underlined lemma are visible; but the strips are far too narrow to show any of
  these reliably, and the same goes for column count and line length.

Tentative interpretations (flagged as such)
- The repeated puncti, "s." tags, a possible "Aug." tag (010 l.4), and what look
  like numerals between puncti (011 l.12, 012 l.8, 015 l.24) suggest continuous
  prose with short citations/references rather than verse or liturgy. I cannot
  tell main text from commentary on this evidence.
- Recurring letter groups that can be read with some confidence across the
  strips: "lex"/"lege"/"leg" (002 l.13, 003 l.14 and l.19, 010 l.12 and l.19,
  011 l.6, l.18, l.23), "vetu" (002 l.15, l.19), "noua(m)" (003 l.15),
  "ſtam(en)ti"/"teſta" (011 l.7, 010 l.15; possibly 003 l.10), "ꝓmitte"
  (010 l.8), "figã" (010 l.1), "pecca" (014 l.25), "in xp" (011 l.19),
  "ꝑfc̃e" (012 l.15), "S(e)c(un)do" (006 l.17). I offer these only as searchable
  letter strings; I have not tried to identify a work and have not filled any gap
  from memory.

SELECTION STATEMENT
- Because each line preserves only a few letters, "connected prose" does not
  exist on these strips. I therefore read EVERY visible line of every tile
  (002-004, 006-008, 010-012, 014-015) rather than selecting spans; the result is
  a line-by-line list of letter groups in vertical order, which is the only
  checkable evidence the strips offer (a source match would have to be tested as
  a vertical "acrostic-like" sequence of mid-line fragments at a constant column
  offset).
- Nothing was left deliberately unread. Lines marked [illegible] or with "?"
  are rubbed or cut on the leaf itself (004 l.5-11, 008 l.5-11, 015 l.22, l.28),
  or (014-015) limited by image scale.

LIMITATIONS
- Every line is cut at both ends; no word boundary at the strip edges is secure,
  and first/last letters are often partial. Many readings rest on minims
  (m/n/u/i) that cannot be divided without context, which I have not supplied.
- Line numbers count from the top of each tile image; overlapping tiles repeat
  lines, and I have marked the repeats ("= image-00N l.X") so they are not
  counted twice.
- Tiles 014 and 015 were viewed at reduced effective resolution (see note
  above); a re-tiling of face D into three or four shorter tiles would improve
  those readings.
- Relationship between the four views (which are recto/verso of which, and the
  order of the strips across the original leaf) is not established. If the
  strips came from the same leaf, a view of them laid side by side, or of the
  host binding, would be the useful next image.
- This is an unverified image reading. I did nothing beyond the rules: no web or
